Ethereum is for shipping.

Here are 22 things the Ethereum ecosystem launched, upgraded, and announced over the past month.

0/ Ethereum hit a new all-time high of 72.8 Million monthly transactions, the highest in network history.

1/ @ethereumfndn, @chainlink, and @Nethermind

6/ This is ongoing work, with contributors continuing to expand coverage, improve tooling, and drive adoption.

Learn more at https://t.co/BsGcYqTHIg

5/ It introduces: 

- ERC-7730: an open standard for human-readable transaction descriptions
- A neutral, mirrorable descriptor registry
- An attestation framework so auditors can verify descriptor integrity (ERC-8176)
- Open developer tooling for wallets, protocols, & auditors
4/ The effort builds on existing clear signing work in the ecosystem, including the approach pioneered by Ledger.

3/ Contributors include Wallets and Hardware (@Ledger, @Trezor, @zknoxhq, @MetaMask, @WalletConnect), Security (@Cyfrin), Infrastructure (@FireblocksHQ, @Zama), Tooling (@Sourcifyeth, @Argotorg), Individual Builders, and the Ethereum Foundation’s Trillion Dollar Security

2/ With clear signing, transactions can be shown in plain language instead of opaque technical data. 

An Ethereum working group is introducing the open approach to fix this.

1/ Today, signing a transaction can still mean approving a string of unreadable hex, otherwise known as “blind signing”.

Blind signing has contributed to billions in ecosystem losses.

0/ Clear signing is now live. 
 
An open standard to end blind signing, making human-readable transactions default. 

This effort brings a major UX and Security upgrade to transaction signing on Ethereum. https://t.co/nIGRCBQh6G

How better rails improve flow:

• more structured transaction data
• cleaner links between payment and business context
• easier tracking from payment to settlement
• less manual stitching across systems

Payments should not become harder to understand after they are made.

Why that is bad for businesses:

• more manual work for finance and ops
• slower reporting and close cycles
• harder tracking across markets and counterparties
• more friction between payment, settlement, and treasury

Why legacy rails make reconciliation harder:

• payment data gets split across providers
• banks and processors separate movement from context
• information is inconsistent
• teams spend time stitching records back together
